summary: Reviewed isActivePipeline and mostRecentEffectivePipeline additions to workflow-helpers.ts. Both functions are well-named, correctly scoped, properly JSDoc-annotated, and consistent with existing module patterns. Logic is sound: isActivePipeline correctly delegates staleness to the pre-existing isStalePipeline helper, and mostRecentEffectivePipeline uses the established auto_cancelled filter pattern. 9 new tests (6 + 3) provide full coverage of specified scenarios. No blocking issues found — PASS.

comments.note: In isActivePipeline (workflow-helpers.ts:357), the guard `if (matching.length === 0) return false;` is redundant — Array.prototype.some() already returns false for empty arrays. The guard is harmless and adds readability context via its comment, but could be removed to reduce cognitive overhead.

isStalePipeline internally checks `pipeline.status !== 'IN_PROGRESS'` as an early-out. Since isActivePipeline pre-filters for IN_PROGRESS before calling isStalePipeline, this status check is always false inside that call path — minor internal redundancy, fully harmless, but worth noting as the two functions evolve.
